objective: Phase 4, registered after the experiments-v3 results and disclosed as such. Phase 3 adopted a 518 px encoder input (G2, 91.6% cross-validated accuracy). Resolution has improved cross-validated accuracy at every step (224, 308, 448 and 518 px); additional views have not (G1). An out-of-fold error review of the phase 2 recipe found 36 of its 39 cross-validation errors in epidermis preparations, and the most confident of them show plain polygonal cells without a visible stomate or crystal. Phase 4 tests whether whole-field texture statistics from patch tokens help at high resolution, and whether the resolution gains continue beyond 518 px, within the same latency budget.
primary_metric: Out-of-fold accuracy from grouped, stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the development pool (train + validation splits).
adoption_rule: Rungs are evaluated in the registered order, each applying its change to the best configuration adopted so far. A rung is adopted if its encoding time fits the latency budget and its out-of-fold accuracy is higher than the current best, or equal with a lower out-of-fold log-loss. Rungs over the latency budget are evaluated and reported but cannot be adopted. Validation, test and held-out results are reported for every rung and are never used to decide adoption.
latency_rationale: Interactive screening: encoding one uploaded image (all views) must take at most 3 s on the reference laptop CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS).

baseline.title: Phase 3 selection (G2): ViT-S/14, 518 px, last-4-block CLS, 4 rotation views
baseline.hypothesis: Reference point carried over from experiments-v3.

ladder.title: Add the mean patch token to last-4-block CLS pooling
ladder.hypothesis: The most confident remaining errors show cell-wall patterns without a salient structure for the CLS tokens to attend to. The mean final-block patch token summarises texture over the whole field as an equally weighted fifth part. At 518 px each patch covers about 8 source pixels, against 19 at 224 px, where patch-mean pooling (E2) was not adopted. Encoding cost is unchanged.

ladder.title: Encoder resolution 588 px with four rotation views
ladder.hypothesis: Tests whether the resolution trend continues: 588 px gives 42 x 42 patches. Extrapolating the measured 448 and 518 px costs gives about 3.0 s per image, so this rung may exceed the latency budget; if so it is reported as an accuracy reference only.

ladder.title: Encoder resolution 588 px with two rotation views
ladder.hypothesis: Encoding two rotations (0 and 90 degrees) keeps 588 px within the budget (about 1.5 s per image estimated) and tests whether the extra resolution outweighs the two fewer views.
